A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EmoEditor and EmoPair research. All 29 pages of v1 and 33 pages of v2, including supplementary material, support comparison. Text, equations, tables and figures can be matched across formatting changes and relocations.

before.justification: V1 reports original quantitative evaluations and ablations in Table 1, online and laboratory human-preference results, and generated-image examples.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results and adds an iteration-sensitivity experiment in supplementary Section S3.3 and Figure S11.

M1.justification: Section 3.2 increases the iterative emotion inference cap from 20 to 30 critic iterations, a limited change to inference stopping. The dual-branch model, conditioning, losses, acceptance criteria and fallback selection remain unchanged. The newly specified encoder layers document the existing component rather than establish a new architecture.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same EmoPair subsets, EmoSet evaluation images, eight emotion categories, within-valence and cross-valence transfers, and neutral MSCOCO examples. The new iteration sweep does not introduce a dataset, task or distinct test scenario.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparator set remains Color Transfer, Neural Style Transfer, CLIP-Styler, InstructPix2Pix and Large Model Series in the quantitative, human-preference and qualitative comparisons. Newly cited works are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The reported inference budget changes from 20 to 30 iterations, and supplementary Section S3.3 introduces a sweep from 1 to 30. The 504-image evaluation set, human-study procedures and four evaluation metrics remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish which retained experiments were rerun under the revised budget.

E4.justification: V2 adds a sensitivity analysis testing how the iteration cap affects emotional alignment and structural deviation, supplementing the existing predictor and alignment-loss ablations. Several qualitative examples are removed, while the online/laboratory comparisons, confusion matrices and explicit failure cases are retained.

E5.justification: V1 presents human-preference point estimates without error bars. V2 adds standard-error bars to Figure 5 and supplementary Figure S7, corresponding to v1 Figure S6. This adds uncertainty reporting without establishing additional participants, repeated runs or seeds.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises ENRD throughout, including Ours from 24.73 to 23.98, and changes the alignment-loss ablation's EMR from 41.12% to 43.35% and ESR from 92.36% to 91.62%. Section 5.1 corrects the stated EMR advantage over LMS from 20 to approximately 39 points. Iteration-response curves are added and qualitative examples removed. Headline EMR/ESR and human-preference percentages remain unchanged; the revised inference budget prevents assuming matched conditions for all table revisions.

T1.justification: The diffusion formulation, noise loss, cosine-alignment loss and metric definitions are retained. Neither version provides theoretical propositions or proofs. Added encoder specifications and conditioning rationale do not introduce new mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and discussion retain the same central contributions: emotion-evoked image generation, EmoEditor, the approximately 340,000-pair EmoPair dataset, four metrics and human evaluation. Claims of competitive superiority and preserving scene semantics and structure are not substantively redefined.

C2.justification: V2 acknowledges favorable evaluation bias from using the emotion predictor P and explains limitations of CLIP-based emotional assessment. It removes v1's incorrect statement that the ablations increase ENRD and ESS, and adds interpretations of the iteration-sensitivity curves. The existing facial-detail and semantic-preservation limitations remain.

D1.justification: New supplementary Section S2.1 specifies the encoder's 8-to-256-to-512-to-768 layers, ReLU activations and final 77-by-768 embedding. Existing initialization, optimizer and GPU details move to S2.2. Public code, model and data release remains a promise; the new checklist additionally states that model users will need to follow usage guidelines.

R1.justification: V2 adds Goetschalckx et al.'s Ganalyze and Widhoelzl and Takmaz's CLIP emotion study to contextualize evaluation, while removing the Ekman citation and six-category example. The main positioning relative to emotion analysis and image editing remains unchanged. Bibliographic updates to retained works are formatting changes.

P1.justification: V2 condenses portions of related work, methods and results, separates the emotion-predictor description, improves supplementary cross-references, and moves filtering and implementation details into the supplement. References move before the supplement and a NeurIPS checklist is appended, but the main six-section narrative and much of its wording remain intact.

P2.justification: The document changes from LNCS-style to NeurIPS-style typography, title/author layout, text area and headers. V2 adds encoder and iteration-analysis figures, redraws preference plots with error bars, and reduces Figure 6 from six examples to two and the supplementary comparison grid from eight to four. Other displays are resized, relocated or renumbered.

improvement.justification: V2 improves reproducibility and evidential transparency through explicit encoder dimensions, iteration-sensitivity results, standard-error bars and acknowledgment of evaluator bias. It also corrects misleading numerical and ablation statements. These are limited gains: several qualitative examples disappear, and the relationship between the revised inference budget and changed table values remains unexplained.
